prompt: A rope is wrapped along the rim of a circular pool of radius $5$ ft, covering a central angle of $2$ radians. How long is that arc of rope, in feet?
hint: Arc length has a beautifully short formula in radians: $s = r\theta$.

hints.text: Arc length has a beautifully short formula in radians: $s = r\theta$.

explanation: When the angle is measured in radians, arc length is simply $s = r\theta$.
Here $r = 5$ ft and $\theta = 2$ radians, so $s = 5 \times 2 = 10$ ft.

alternativeExplanations.title: What a radian really is
steps: One radian is exactly the angle that wraps one radius-length of arc around the rim.
So 2 radians wraps 2 radius-lengths of arc: $2 \times 5 = 10$ ft.
